rationale: Evidence: the baseline left the track on every development trial (60/60 off_track, 0 finishes). Max error was about 0.062 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, and line_loss_events averaged about 1 per run. Progress was 0.49 on the oval, 0.22 on the s-bend and 0.11 on the slalom, so the robot is failing on bends, not stalling. The likely causes are (a) speed too high for the turn radius, so the robot overshoots and the tape leaves the 80 mm sensor span, and (b) too little damping, since kd 0.3 is low for kp 2.0. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.6 to 1.3, the largest safe step I can justify without evidence of the speed-to-time mapping; a score without completion still earns up to about 440 from progress and tracking, so staying on track matters more than the 3.0 s limit right now. (2) kp 2.0 to 1.6 to reduce overshoot on bends. (3) kd 0.3 to 0.5 to damp the swing. (4) Sensor span widened from x = ±0.04 to ±0.06 (step 0.03 m, sensor size 0.012) so the line stays under a sensor on sharper bends and line loss events should fall. Weights stay -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 with the correct sign convention. Expected result: fewer or no off-track ends, progress above 0.5 on the s-bend and slalom, and a first finish possible on the oval. Hypotheses to test: line loss is mainly due to the narrow sensor span; speed is the main driver of max_error. Measurements wanted next: max_error and line_loss_events per track, progress, and completion_time, so I can judge whether base_speed should rise toward 1.5 to meet the 3.0 s limit.
